items.title: Toshiko Akiyoshi interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 17, 1999
items.q: Charlie Rice, the drummer, I forgot the name of the guitar player, they didn’t have a pianist for the USO tour, because the piano you know is not always there, so they didn’t usually have a pianist. ctx.x: So Teddy Wilson — now I think I had read that you had a chance encounter with Oscar Peterson?

Yes. The first great pianist I had met actually in person was Oscar Peterson. That was in 1953 I believe. That was the first time the American jazz group came to Japan for the Japanese audience. Before that a few groups came to Japan but they were for the USO © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-

tour for the American troops. For example, Louis Armstrong was there one time, and the Gene Krupa Trio was there one time, and way before that, in 1950 I believe there was a dance band, Les Brown’s band with Bob Hope. But more than anything, I think ’51, I’m not quite sure, there is Oscar Pettiford the leader, and J.J. Johnson and Howard McGhee, they were also on the USO tour.
